front-matter: How to read this book, the map he drew himself on SRKWorld.com in 2000, and the whole arc in ten movements.
prologue: "If not for Shah Rukh Khan…": the sentence that started the thesis, and why 4 October 2021 at Mannat is where it all begins.
chapter-01: His father, a Quit India prisoner from Peshawar, stays in Delhi after Partition. The boy is born into that inheritance in 1965.
chapter-02: St. Columba's, the Sword of Honour, hockey and the school play. A star pupil shaped by his teachers, and a father lost in 1981.
chapter-03: Economics at Hansraj on paper, Barry John's Theatre Action Group in practice: the rehearsal room where the actor was trained.
chapter-04: Fauji and Circus make him a household face on Doordarshan. His mother dies; he marries Gauri and moves to Bombay.
chapter-05: Four films in his first year, the villain of Baazigar and Darr, then DDLJ. The new middle class finds its hero.
chapter-06: Dreamz Unlimited, Aryan Infomatics and SRKWorld.com, launched 14 November 2000: a star's own portal before India had broadband.
chapter-07: Shah Rock Jaan, the cartoon self drawn for a computer screen, and G.One, the hero who stepped out of the code in 2011.
chapter-08: Red Chillies, Red Chillies VFX and the Kolkata Knight Riders: the star starts building institutions around himself.
chapter-09: He joins Twitter as @iamsrk and sells My Name Is Khan through it. The star becomes the platform.
chapter-10: Ra.One: games, merchandise, comics, 25+ brands and G.One. Indian cinema's boldest attempt to build a digital kingdom.
chapter-11: The 2000 plan beside the 2011 campaign: what SRKWorld aimed for, what Ra.One delivered, and what never came.
chapter-12: Chennai Express asks its audience to drive: the tweet-powered train, games, karaoke and daily analytics, from the case study.
chapter-13: Same strategist, same star, two years apart. Ra.One built a universe; Chennai Express built a movement.
chapter-14: 2014 to 2018 film by film, from Happy New Year to Zero. The money held up; the system around the films did not.
chapter-15: The box-office graph from My Name Is Khan to Dunki: no film of 2014 to 2018 reached the Chennai Express level.
chapter-16: What the technology was asked to do: a product in its own right, then single tie-ins, then platform features.
chapter-17: Why the virtual train never became a railway: five possible explanations, the evidence for each, and what is missing.
chapter-18: Five conclusions on the lull: ambition, benchmark, innovations without the architecture, Zero the exception, and the gap.
chapter-19: 2019 to 2021, the years without a film: the balcony, the pandemic help, and a silence the public read for itself.
chapter-20: October 2021 in the public record, in order, with nothing added, beside the author's recollection of 4 October.
chapter-21: Of the four weeks between raid and homecoming, almost nothing is public. What is documented, and what this book won't invent.
chapter-22: The central metaphor: Asoka laid down the sword; this King laid down the microphone. The three acts of Be Da Boo-Da.
chapter-23: The comeback starts on his birthday with the Pathaan teaser, survives a third boycott, and makes silence the campaign.
chapter-24: Jawan: a record opening day, ₹1,148.32 crore worldwide and his first National Film Award for Best Actor.
chapter-25: Dunki, the quietest of the three: a migrant story told in "Drops" from his 58th birthday. After fire, tears.
chapter-26: Three films in eleven months, about ₹2,669 crore: the numbers of the resurrection, with both counts shown.
chapter-27: From the Hyundai Santro (1998) to Visa (2026): 35+ brands, the Cadbury AI ad, and what his name is worth.
chapter-28: The Burj Khalifa trailer, #BeMyGuest, Royal Estates and the Shahrukhz tower: the city that bought into the face.
chapter-29: Three IPL titles, five in the Caribbean, teams in the US and UAE, and a cricket ground of their own in Los Angeles.
chapter-30: Hurun's estimates, from ₹7,300 crore in 2024 to about ₹12,490 crore in 2025, and Red Chillies' own filed figures.
chapter-31: What he owns or backs, from Red Chillies to Flam: he doesn't only act in the business of attention, he builds it.
chapter-32: He invests in Flam, a US$40 million AI interactive-content company. The ghost of Ra.One meets the AI era.
chapter-33: In 2026 the broadband, phones and tools SRKWorld lacked are in every hand. His career read through S.T.E.A.M.
chapter-34: Proposal: SRKWorld reborn as a fan-franchising operating system, where fan communities create and earn together.
chapter-35: Proposal: ijOO, the author's own universe, and the AI Bioskope, a cinema fans make without borrowing anyone's face.
chapter-36: Fans already make KING with AI. Inquilaab and #FreeMyFace: fans fighting for a star's rights over his own face.
chapter-37: How KING became his film, the title reveal on his 60th birthday, and the hype before the 24 December 2026 release.
chapter-38: Robert Downey Jr. and Shah Rukh Khan, both born in 1965, open six days apart. The trade wants a clash; this is a relay.
chapter-39: The author's synthesis: five cards (KING, brands, Hurun, Knight Riders, Flam), one King. Not renouncing; doubling down.
chapter-40: Proposal: Check Mate Fire, the author's 36-piece chess on an 81-square board where the pawn becomes the lighter.
chapter-41: 43,400 new posts and 7.5 million views in a day, with no official campaign. The fans are already running it.
chapter-42: Proposal: the Third Wheel, a campaign in which he is the charming friend in a fan couple's story.
chapter-43: There is a film, a business empire and an audience. The evidence gives us the cards; it does not reveal the hand.
chapter-44: Proposal: O TO X, the reader's game. Start at zero, pick a route, add a tile of your own life, and build your X.
chapter-45: Proposal: MY SUM, the Royal Flush Challenge. Players combine what they made into one universe, credited to all.
chapter-46: What you can play today on agarmainkinghota.com, from posters to Chess81 and King's Lairs, and what comes next.

addendum-b: What earlier drafts said, what the evidence says, and the source for each correction.
addendum-c: Every dated event from 1946 to 2026 in one table, with the chapter where it is told.
addendum-d: Every film from 1992 to 2023, his role, and whether his own company made it.
addendum-e: Eight Filmfare Best Actor awards, the Padma Shri, the Légion d'honneur, the National Award for Jawan and more.
addendum-f: What each campaign claim rests on, and how strong the evidence is, from documented to recollection.
addendum-g: Every [Unverified] claim in one register: what is needed to prove it, and who can supply it.
addendum-h: The principal sources behind the book, and where every picture comes from.
final-frame: We built the campaigns, watched the comeback, celebrated the resurrection. What did October 2021 ask of us?
